subtype_selection.rationale: HER2+ selected over IBC, male BC, and metaplastic BC due to: (1) maximal dome pathway connectivity — HER2 is the canonical activator of the dome's central PI3K/AKT axis; HER2 amplification drives ER stress and ATF6 engagement at the protein-folding level; emerging BRCAness/HRD in HER2+ connects to TNBC RAD51 dome knowledge; (2) highest unmet clinical need — T-DXd antibody-drug conjugate era creates new resistance questions entirely distinct from existing TNBC PARPi / ILC endocrine resistance dome hypotheses; (3) population size — HER2+ is ~15-20% of all breast cancers vs <1% for metaplastic or ~1% for male BC; (4) zero semantic overlap with any existing dome hypothesis — existing 11 hypotheses are ILC-specific (CDH1/ferroptosis/endocrine resistance/ESR1) or TNBC-specific (BRCA1 methylation/HRD/RAD51); HER2+ is mechanistically orthogonal.

pathway_connections_to_dome.PI3K_AKT: HER2 dimerization is the canonical activator of PI3K p110alpha via p85 adapter — directly extends dome hyp-ilc-006 (CDH1-loss PI3Ka liberation) into a HER2-driven PI3K activation context

candidates.hypothesis: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) payload delivery of topoisomerase I inhibitor (DXd) to HER2+ breast cancer cells induces ferroptosis as a co-lethal mechanism alongside its established DNA damage/apoptosis pathway — specifically by depleting GSH precursors through DXd-induced mitochondrial dysfunction that suppresses the cystine/glutamate transporter SLC7A11 (xCT) at the post-translational level. HER2+ tumors with low baseline SLC7A11 expression are therefore disproportionately sensitive to T-DXd, while HER2+ tumors with high SLC7A11 expression (the 'ferroptosis-escape' phenotype) acquire partial T-DXd resistance via ferroptosis evasion independent of topoisomerase I mutation or drug efflux. SLC7A11 protein expression by IHC in pre-treatment HER2+ biopsies predicts T-DXd clinical benefit, stratifying HER2+ patients into ferroptosis-competent (SLC7A11-low, high T-DXd sensitivity) versus ferroptosis-escaped (SLC7A11-high, lower T-DXd sensitivity and early resistance) populations.
candidates.mechanism: DXd (the exatecan derivative payload in T-DXd) inhibits topoisomerase I, causing DNA replication fork collapse and mitochondrial DNA damage. Mitochondrial damage suppresses Complex I/III electron transport, increasing ROS and lipid peroxidation — conditions that trigger ferroptosis when GPX4 activity is insufficient. In HER2+ cells, HER2→PI3K→AKT normally phosphorylates and activates NRF2, which transcriptionally upregulates SLC7A11 and GPX4 as a pro-survival anti-ferroptosis program. When T-DXd is delivered and HER2 is internalized with the ADC, HER2 signaling is transiently suppressed at the membrane; the DXd payload simultaneously generates mitochondrial ROS. The net effect: NRF2-driven SLC7A11/GPX4 transcription drops (HER2 internalized → PI3K/NRF2 reduced) while ROS load rises (DXd mitochondrial damage) — creating a ferroptosis execution window. Cells that pre-adapt by constitutively high SLC7A11 expression (independent of HER2/PI3K input) escape this window, representing the ferroptosis-escape resistance mechanism.
candidates.testable_experiment: Two-component experiment: (1) T-DXd dose-response in HER2+ cell panel stratified by SLC7A11 expression (BT-474, SKBR3, HCC1954, AU565) — correlate IC50 with baseline SLC7A11 IHC/Western, test ferrostatin-1 rescue (ferroptosis inhibitor) to isolate ferroptotic component of T-DXd killing; (2) SLC7A11 overexpression in T-DXd-sensitive HER2+ lines (BT-474 SLC7A11-OE) — test if SLC7A11 OE reduces T-DXd sensitivity in a ferrostatin-1-recapitulable manner. Lipid peroxidation readout: C11-BODIPY flow cytometry after T-DXd treatment. Mitochondrial ROS: MitoSOX staining. Validation endpoint: T-DXd-treated HER2+ patient FFPE biopsies (available from DESTINY-Breast01/03 trial biobanks) — SLC7A11 IHC H-score vs PFS/ORR correlation.

candidates.hypothesis: HER2 gene amplification constitutively saturates ER protein folding capacity by producing excess HER2 protein (15-30x normal), constitutively activating the ATF6 branch of the unfolded protein response (UPR) as a survival adaptation. This chronic ATF6 activation in HER2+ tumors pre-arms the FBXO24 E3 ubiquitin ligase axis (established in dome as an ATF6 transcriptional target) and simultaneously elevates GRP78/BiP as a HER2 chaperone, making GRP78 both a direct HER2 stability factor AND an ATF6-driven pro-survival effector. Trastuzumab resistance in HER2+ breast cancer is therefore in part a consequence of GRP78 upregulation (buffering HER2 protein from trastuzumab-induced ER-stress-mediated degradation), and GRP78 inhibitor (HA15 or MKT-077) co-treatment with trastuzumab is predicted to collapse this resistance by simultaneously withdrawing HER2 chaperone support and sensitizing cells to HER2-targeted therapy-induced ER stress.
candidates.mechanism: HER2 (ERBB2) is a receptor tyrosine kinase synthesized and folded in the ER. In HER2-amplified tumors, the massive overproduction of HER2 protein chronically loads the ER folding machinery, constitutively activating ATF6 (and to lesser extent IRE1/PERK UPR branches). ATF6 transcriptionally upregulates GRP78/HSPA5 as the primary HER2 chaperone — a process reported in trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ models (Cook 2012). ATF6 also transcriptionally upregulates FBXO24 (the dome's established BRCAness-inducing E3 ligase from PMID 40764992). In the HER2+ context, FBXO24 likely targets not only RAD51 but also HER2-ubiquitination pathway components — potentially competing with HER2 stabilization signals. The net survival outcome is: constitutive UPR/ATF6 activation → GRP78 elevation (HER2 stability) + FBXO24 elevation (DNA repair destabilization) simultaneously. Trastuzumab disrupts HER2 surface signaling but cannot efficiently clear HER2 protein if GRP78 is providing ER retention/stabilization. GRP78 inhibition (HA15) destabilizes HER2 protein at the ER level, amplifying trastuzumab-induced HER2 depletion and simultaneously forcing the cell into irresolvable ER stress — a synthetic lethality that exploits the constitutive ATF6 addiction of HER2+ tumors.
candidates.testable_experiment: Three-arm experiment in trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ models (BT-474-TrasR, JIMT-1): (1) ATF6 ChIP-seq to confirm ATF6 occupancy at GRP78/HSPA5 and FBXO24 promoters in HER2-amplified vs HER2-normal cells — verify constitutive ATF6 activation signature; (2) HA15 (GRP78 inhibitor) + trastuzumab combination viability assay (SynergyFinder matrix) vs trastuzumab alone in BT-474-TrasR and JIMT-1 cells; expected synergy in GRP78-high trastuzumab-resistant but not in GRP78-low trastuzumab-sensitive lines; (3) HER2 protein stability assay: cycloheximide chase in trastuzumab-resistant cells ± HA15 — predict faster HER2 degradation with GRP78 inhibition. Pharmacodynamic readout: GRP78 protein levels by Western, ATF6 nuclear fraction by subcellular fractionation. Validation: TCGA HER2+ proteomics (CPTAC HER2+ cohort) — HSPA5 protein expression correlation with trastuzumab resistance phenotype and FBXO24 protein levels.

evidence.relevance: Direct evidence that GRP78 elevation drives trastuzumab resistance in HER2+ BC; mechanistic basis for GRP78 inhibitor co-treatment hypothesis

candidates.novelty_claim: No published study has integrated ATF6-driven FBXO24 (dome knowledge from TNBC) with GRP78-driven trastuzumab resistance in HER2+ breast cancer as a unified constitutive UPR addiction model. The proposal that HER2 amplification creates constitutive ATF6 activation that simultaneously elevates GRP78 (HER2 stability) and FBXO24 (DNA repair destabilization), and that GRP78 inhibition collapses both arms, is a novel mechanistic synthesis. Prior work (Cook 2012) established GRP78 in trastuzumab resistance without the ATF6/FBXO24 connection; dome hyp-tnbc-004 established ATF6/FBXO24 in TNBC BRCAness without the HER2/GRP78 connection — this hypothesis is the novel cross-subtype synthesis.
candidates.actionability: Actionable in 6-12 months: HA15 (GRP78 inhibitor) is a validated research compound with published TNBC/pancreatic cancer preclinical data; BT-474-TrasR (trastuzumab-resistant) and JIMT-1 are established cell models. ATF6 ChIP-seq is technically feasible. Translational path: GRP78 IHC as companion diagnostic for trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ BC; HA15 + trastuzumab combination is a Phase 1-ready hypothesis if HA15 advances clinically.
candidates.dome_connection: Directly imports dome ATF6→FBXO24 axis (hyp-tnbc-002 and hyp-tnbc-004) to HER2+ subtype via constitutive UPR hypothesis; extends dome's ATF6 as BRCAness regulator concept to protein folding/chaperone resistance in HER2+ — maximizes dome knowledge transfer efficiency

iupac_semantic_overlap_estimates.note: Highest overlap vs hyp-tnbc-004 (both involve ATF6 in breast cancer resistance) and hyp-tnbc-002 (both involve FBXO24); mechanistic distinction is HER2 amplification as constitutive ATF6 activator + GRP78 chaperone resistance mechanism vs pharmacological ATF6 activation by ivabradine in TNBC — different subtype, different upstream trigger, different downstream output (GRP78/chaperone vs mRNA stabilization)

candidates.hypothesis: In HER2+ breast cancer with acquired resistance to trastuzumab+pertuzumab (dual HER2 blockade), ERBB3 (HER3) acts as a PI3Kα-bypass adapter that restores PI3K/AKT signaling through ERBB3's unique p85-binding motif — independent of ERBB2 kinase activity — by partnering with alternative kinase inputs (IGF1R, MET, FGFR) that phosphorylate ERBB3's cytoplasmic tail at Y1289/Y1328 without requiring ERBB2 transactivation. This ERBB3-mediated PI3K bypass is the dominant resistance mechanism in the ~40% of trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ tumors that retain ERBB3 expression with concurrent IGF1R or MET co-amplification, predicting that dual HER2+IGF1R or HER2+MET co-inhibition (not pan-PI3K inhibition) is required to overcome resistance — because pan-PI3K inhibition bypasses ERBB3 but fails to prevent the receptor-level PI3K re-engagement that drives resistance.
candidates.mechanism: ERBB3 is the dominant PI3K activator in the ERBB receptor network: ERBB3's cytoplasmic tail contains 6 YXXM motifs that directly bind the PI3K p85 regulatory subunit, making ERBB3-PI3K coupling 100x more efficient than ERBB2-PI3K coupling. In the normal HER2+ signaling context, ERBB2 transactivates ERBB3 by phosphorylating ERBB3's Y1289/Y1328, which then recruits p85. Trastuzumab+pertuzumab blocks HER2-ERBB3 dimerization, reducing ERBB3 phosphorylation — the primary intended mechanism. Resistance arises when IGF1R or MET (which are frequently co-amplified in HER2+ BC) provide an alternative kinase input to ERBB3, phosphorylating the same YXXM tyrosines through cross-receptor transphosphorylation. The ERBB3 adapter is retained (ERBB3 is not mutated in resistance); only its upstream activating kinase switches from HER2 to IGF1R/MET. Pan-PI3K inhibition (alpelisib/copanlisib) targets the effector but not the receptor-level bypass — cells re-engage PI3K through continuous ERBB3 re-phosphorylation. Dual inhibition of HER2 + IGF1R or HER2 + MET targets the resistance kinase that re-activates ERBB3, thereby collapsing the bypass.
candidates.testable_experiment: Phosphoproteomic time-series in trastuzumab+pertuzumab-resistant HER2+ cell lines (JIMT-1, HCC1954-TrasR) co-expressing IGF1R or MET amplification: (1) ERBB3 phosphorylation (pY1289) by ELISA after trastuzumab+pertuzumab treatment — confirm ERBB3 pY1289 persists in resistant vs sensitive lines; (2) IGF1R inhibitor (linsitinib) or MET inhibitor (tepotinib) treatment: does it reduce ERBB3 pY1289 and AKT-pS473 in the resistant lines? (3) Triple combination: trastuzumab + pertuzumab + linsitinib or tepotinib — predict synergy only in IGF1R-high or MET-high resistant lines, not in resistant lines driven by PIK3CA mutation (where the bypass is post-ERBB3). Validation: ERBB3 pY1289 + IGF1R/MET protein by IHC in trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ patient biopsies (CLEOPATRA trial progression samples) — correlation with subsequent PI3K-pathway inhibitor response.

evidence.citation: Garrett JT et al., Clin Cancer Res 2011 (and Sergina 2007 Nature) — ERBB3 is a critical adapter for HER2-driven PI3K activation; ERBB3 phosphorylation is required for maximal PI3K/AKT signaling in HER2+ BC; ERBB3 upregulation is a common resistance mechanism to ERBB2 inhibitors
evidence.relevance: Establishes ERBB3 as PI3K adapter in HER2+ BC and confirmed resistance mechanism; alternative kinase input to ERBB3 is the novel extension

evidence.citation: Chakrabarty A et al., Cancer Cell 2012 — IGF1R co-activation drives trastuzumab resistance in HER2+ BC; IGF1R/ERBB2 cross-talk at the membrane; dual IGF1R+HER2 targeting overcomes resistance in preclinical models
evidence.relevance: Direct evidence for IGF1R as alternative kinase in trastuzumab resistance; the ERBB3 transphosphorylation mechanism is the novel synthesis linking IGF1R resistance to PI3K bypass via ERBB3 rather than direct IGF1R→PI3K

evidence.citation: Sheng Q et al., Cancer Discov 2010 — MET amplification drives trastuzumab resistance in HER2+ gastric/breast cancer; MET inhibitor re-sensitizes resistant models; MET-HER2 co-amplification identified in ~5-10% of HER2+ BC
evidence.relevance: Establishes MET as alternative resistance kinase in HER2+ BC; the ERBB3 transphosphorylation model unifies MET and IGF1R resistance under a common ERBB3-adapter mechanism

evidence.citation: Piccolo E et al., Oncogene 2019 — ERBB3 YXXM motifs directly recruit PI3K p85; ERBB3 is required for maximal PI3K activation in ERBB receptor network; ERBB3 mutation is rare but ERBB3 overexpression is common in HER2+ resistance
evidence.relevance: Establishes ERBB3's p85-binding motifs as PI3K engagement mechanism; supports adapter-bypass model where ERBB3 tail remains as PI3K recruiter even after HER2 is blocked

evidence.note: Recent 2024-2025 ERBB3 transphosphorylation by IGF1R/MET data not retrievable; hypothesis is mechanistic synthesis of ERBB3 p85-binding literature + IGF1R/MET trastuzumab resistance literature

candidates.novelty_claim: The specific mechanistic model that IGF1R or MET transphosphorylates ERBB3's YXXM motifs to restore p85/PI3K recruitment after HER2 blockade — making ERBB3 an 'orphan PI3K adapter' that alternative kinases can hijack — has not been proposed as a unified mechanism. Prior work studied IGF1R and MET resistance in HER2+ independently; the ERBB3 transphosphorylation model is the unifying connector. The therapeutic corollary (dual HER2+IGF1R or HER2+MET is superior to pan-PI3K inhibition specifically in ERBB3-dependent bypass) is a novel clinical prediction. This is mechanistically distinct from dome hyp-ilc-006 (CDH1-loss PI3Ka liberation is a constitutive structural mechanism; this is a resistance-acquired receptor-level bypass via alternative kinase transphosphorylation).
candidates.actionability: Actionable in 12-18 months: tepotinib (MET inhibitor) and linsitinib (IGF1R inhibitor) are clinical-stage compounds; trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ cell lines and patient-derived organoids are available; CLEOPATRA trial biobank material may contain HER2+ progression biopsies with available IGF1R/MET IHC. Phase 2 basket trial: HER2+ progressed on trastuzumab+pertuzumab, stratified by ERBB3 pY1289 + IGF1R/MET amplification — randomize to tucatinib+capmatinib vs tucatinib+alpelisib.
candidates.dome_connection: Extends dome hyp-ilc-006 (CDH1-loss PI3Ka liberation) — both are PI3K bypass mechanisms in breast cancer resistance but via structurally distinct routes (constitutive CDH1-loss PI3Ka liberation vs acquired ERBB3-adapter alternative kinase bypass); HER2+ PI3K axis enriches dome's PI3K pathway coverage from ILC to HER2+ context with a new mechanistic archetype

Unifies two published resistance mechanisms (IGF1R resistance, MET resistance) under one molecular model — high explanatory power per hypothesis unit

Clear therapeutic prediction: HER2+IGF1Ri or HER2+METi (receptor-level) > pan-PI3Ki (effector-level) in ERBB3-dependent bypass — immediately testable and differentiates from current alpelisib-based approaches

weaknesses: ERBB3 YXXM transphosphorylation by IGF1R (vs direct IGF1R→PI3K activation) requires direct biochemical evidence; phosphoproteomics may not distinguish ERBB3 transphosphorylation from direct IGF1R→p85 binding as the PI3K activation route

winner.hypothesis: T-DXd payload delivery depletes SLC7A11-mediated ferroptosis protection in HER2+ breast cancer by transiently suppressing HER2→PI3K→NRF2→SLC7A11 signaling during HER2 internalization while simultaneously generating mitochondrial ROS via DXd topoisomerase I inhibition, creating a ferroptosis execution window that is escaped in SLC7A11-high tumors — making SLC7A11 IHC expression a predictive biomarker stratifying T-DXd benefit in HER2+ breast cancer.
winner.testable_experiment: T-DXd dose-response in HER2+ cell panel (BT-474, SKBR3, HCC1954, AU565) stratified by SLC7A11 expression; ferrostatin-1 rescue to isolate ferroptotic killing component; C11-BODIPY lipid peroxidation as pharmacodynamic readout; DESTINY-Breast01/03 biobank SLC7A11 IHC vs PFS correlation.
winner.why_winner: Highest combined score driven by novelty (0.87 — no published T-DXd/SLC7A11/ferroptosis connection) and importance (0.88 — T-DXd is the most active HER2+ BC therapy and resistance prediction is a major unmet need in DESTINY-Breast era). Actionability is high (0.85) because DESTINY-Breast biobanks exist, ferrostatin-1 rescue is a clean mechanistic probe, and SLC7A11 IHC is a validated assay from dome hyp-ilc-003 work.
